[USER] User is considering going on a low-carb diet to lose weight.  
[USER] User is confused with conflicting information about diets.  
[USER] User feels frustrated with their weight loss progress.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Different types of diets can have varying impacts on an individual's overall mental and physical health.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Mediterranean Diet: Linked to lower risk of heart disease, stroke, cognitive decline, weight loss, and reducing inflammation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ketogenic Diet: High in fat, moderate in protein, low in carbohydrates; helps with weight loss and blood sugar control but may cause fatigue, constipation, and bad breath.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Vegan Diet: Excludes all animal products; can lower cholesterol and heart disease risk but may lead to nutrient deficiencies if not planned properly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Paleo Diet: Based on early human foods; can help with weight loss and inflammation but may lack essential nutrients.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Gluten-Free Diet: Excludes gluten; necessary for celiac disease but may have no added benefits for others and could lead to fiber deficiency.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The best diet includes a variety of whole, nutritious foods and is balanced in macronutrients.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Consult with a healthcare professional or registered dietitian to determine the best diet for specific needs and health goals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Consider health goals, health history, evaluate evidence, listen to your body, and seek advice from a registered dietitian when choosing a diet.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for a low-carb diet: Choose healthy fats, don't neglect protein, focus on nutrient-dense carbohydrates, increase water intake, and monitor your body's response.  
[USER] User appreciates the helpful tips provided by the assistant.  
[USER] User plans to consult with a registered dietitian before starting any new diet.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommendations for finding a reputable registered dietitian: Ask your doctor, search online, check with insurance, look for credentials (RD), and read reviews.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Registered dietitians should listen to needs, understand health goals, and provide evidence-based recommendations.  
[USER] User is tempted to try fad diets that promise quick weight loss.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fad diets are not recommended as they often promise quick results but can be harmful and lead to yo-yo dieting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Instead of fad diets, focus on sustainable, healthy changes to lifestyle, including a balanced diet and regular exercise.
